_note: Traditional peoples of the Nigerian nations other than the Igbo, for the registry.
Proposed by a model and then checked by a second pass that was told to reject anything
it could not place: a town, a dialect, a quarter or a family is not a people, and an
invented people is worse than a missing one. Names the check could not place are
The owner's ruling is that the registry is not only Igbo. These entries carry their
nation in `nation`, so the section can group and filter by it.

peoples.name: Ife
peoples.summary: Found in Osun State and known as the ancient spiritual cradle of the Yoruba civilization.

peoples.name: Oyo
peoples.summary: Found mainly in Oyo State and renowned for the historic military and political legacy of the old Oyo Empire.

peoples.name: Ohori
peoples.summary: Found in Ogun State and the Republic of Benin, known for rich agricultural traditions and borderland heritage.

peoples.name: Ekiti
peoples.summary: Found in Ekiti State and celebrated for its rolling hills, high level of education, and distinct sub-dialect.

peoples.name: Ife-Togo
peoples.summary: Found in Togo and recognized as an external diaspora branch maintaining deep Yoruba ancestral ties.

peoples.name: Oworo
peoples.summary: Found in Kogi State along the banks of the Niger River, known for a unique culture blending Yoruba and central Nigerian influences.

peoples.name: Akoko
peoples.summary: Found in Ondo State and known for extreme linguistic and cultural diversity within a compact geographic area.

peoples.name: Ijesa
peoples.summary: Found in Osun State and famed for historical trading prowess, rich cultural festivals, and industrious craftsmanship.

peoples.name: Egba
peoples.summary: Found in Ogun State and historically prominent in Nigerian commerce, education, and early print media.

peoples.name: Ijebu
peoples.summary: Found in Ogun State and celebrated for ancient commercial acumen, historic defensive walls, and distinct age-grade systems.

peoples.name: Ondo
peoples.summary: Found in Ondo State and known for a centralized monarchy and cocoa farming heritage.

peoples.name: Owo
peoples.summary: Found in Ondo State and renowned for world-class ivory carving and ancient artistic traditions influenced by Benin and Ife.

peoples.name: Igbomina
peoples.summary: Found in Kwara and Osun States, traditionally recognized for agricultural skill and woodcarving artistry.

peoples.name: Ketu
peoples.summary: Found across Ogun State and the Republic of Benin, noted for ancient kingship traditions and resilient cultural identity.

peoples.name: Ede
peoples.summary: Found in Osun State and historically established as a military outpost for the old Oyo Empire.

peoples.name: Ijesha
peoples.summary: Found in Osun State, representing an alternate spelling variant of the Ijesa people.

peoples.name: Ijumu
peoples.summary: Found in Kogi State and known for blending Yoruba cultural elements with the traditions of central Nigeria.

peoples.name: Yagba
peoples.summary: Found in Kogi and Kwara States, historically noted for iron-working and agricultural productivity.

peoples.name: Bunu
peoples.summary: Found in Kogi State, known for close historical ties to neighboring central Nigerian groups while retaining a Yoruba identity.

peoples.name: Ibadan
peoples.summary: Found in Oyo State and famed as a 19th-century military powerhouse that became a massive urban center.

peoples.name: Awori
peoples.summary: Found in Lagos and Ogun States, traditionally recognized as the original settlers of the Lagos coastal swampland.

peoples.name: Nembe
peoples.summary: Found in Bayelsa State and celebrated for maritime history, ancient trading states, and rich mangrove ecology.

peoples.name: Kalabari
peoples.summary: Found in Rivers State and renowned for powerful canoe house trading kingdoms and coastal commerce.

peoples.name: Okrika
peoples.summary: Found in Rivers State and known for seafaring prowess and strategic island settlements.

peoples.name: Boma
peoples.summary: Found across the riverine areas of Bayelsa and Rivers States, known for fishing and creek navigation.

peoples.name: Beni
peoples.summary: Found in Edo State and globally famous for the great Benin Empire, bronze casting, and a highly structured monarchy.

peoples.name: Esan
peoples.summary: Found in Edo State and known for agricultural achievements and numerous autonomous chiefdoms.

peoples.name: Etsako
peoples.summary: Found in Edo State and recognized for diverse linguistic sub-groups inhabiting the northern part of the state.

peoples.name: Owan
peoples.summary: Found in Edo State and known for rich forest resources and vibrant cultural festivals.

peoples.name: Akoko-Edo
peoples.summary: Found in Edo State and famous for possessing one of the highest concentrations of distinct languages in Nigeria.

peoples.name: Urhobo
peoples.summary: Found in Delta State and renowned for palm produce production, oil wealth, and decentralized democratic kingdoms.

peoples.name: Isoko
peoples.summary: Found in Delta State and celebrated for farming, fishing, and rich spiritual folklore.

peoples.name: Itsekiri
peoples.summary: Found in Delta State and known for the revered Olu of Warri institution and a history of early European contact.

peoples.name: Igala
peoples.summary: Found mainly in Kogi State along the Niger-Benue confluence, led by the Attah Igala and known for rich historical kingdoms.

peoples.name: Ebira
peoples.summary: Found in Kogi State and renowned for industrious textile weaving, vibrant masquerade festivals, and commerce.

peoples.name: Nupe
peoples.summary: Found in Niger State and famous for the majestic Nupe Kingdom, river transport, and intricate glass bead artistry.

peoples.name: Idoma
peoples.summary: Found in Benue State and celebrated for the rich Alekwu ancestral worship and agricultural excellence.

peoples.name: Tiv
peoples.summary: Found in Benue State and renowned as the food basket of Nigeria through extensive yam farming and egalitarian social structures.

peoples.name: Efik
peoples.summary: Found in Cross River State and celebrated for maritime trade, rich culinary arts, and the famous Ekpe secret society.

peoples.name: Ibibio
peoples.summary: Found in Akwa Ibom State and recognized for ancient civilization, wood carving, and agricultural abundance.
